palette.role: Ground-level evergreen and winter fragrance beside shaded approaches. Not a climber.

attachment.supportNeeds: A shaded soil bed near a path. No climbing surface.

wood.basis: Inferred; no source states it for Sarcococca. The flowers open from late December to February (Bean, Trees and Shrubs Online), when no new growth has been made since autumn, so they are carried on shoots of the season before. The RHS says the same of another winter-flowering evergreen group, the Cirrhosa clematis ("on the previous year's growth"), and puts this shrub in pruning group 8, pruned if at all straight after flowering.

monthsUK.basis: Bean (Trees and Shrubs Online): the flowers "are borne from late December to February". Stated in months. The RHS record says winter, the same three months.

flowering.display: Small cream-white, highly scented flowers; black berries.

site.soil: Humus-rich, moist but well-drained; tolerates dry shade once established.

management.notes: Maintain access and form; mulch and water while establishing. The RHS height field says 1-1.5 m while its description says to 2 m.

hazards: Potentially harmful; fruit is ornamental and not to be eaten (RHS).

sources.label: RHS: pruning evergreen shrubs (pruning groups 8 to 10)
Trees and Shrubs Online (Bean): Sarcococca confusa
